intro: Searching for ADHD counselling near you usually means you want someone local who understands how ADHD affects daily life — whether you have a diagnosis already or are still working out what is going on. You might be looking for help with focus, emotions, routines or relationships, or simply a space to talk things through. We can introduce you to a counsellor in your area who works with ADHD, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for ADHD counselling near me often need
need_lead: The reasons people look for ADHD counselling close to home tend to be practical and personal at the same time.
needs: You have a diagnosis of ADHD and want help with organisation, motivation or the day-to-day impact it has on work and home life.
You recognise ADHD traits in yourself but have not been assessed, and you want somewhere to talk things through before deciding what to do next.
You feel overwhelmed by emotions, rejection or frustration and want a regular space to make sense of them with someone who understands ADHD.
ADHD is affecting your relationships, and you want support in communicating better with a partner, family or colleagues.
You are looking for someone you can see in person nearby, because travelling far or meeting online does not suit you.
context: ADHD counselling and coaching can help with organisation, emotions and the impact of ADHD on work and relationships, whether that is before or after a diagnosis. Coaching is not a diagnosis, and strategies you learn in sessions are there to help with daily life rather than replace medical care. Decisions about medication are a separate medical matter, so it is worth keeping that in mind when you think about what you want from counselling.

"Counsellor" and "psychotherapist" are not protected titles in the UK, so it pays to check how someone is registered. Choosing a practitioner on a register accredited by the Professional Standards Authority, such as BACP, UKCP or NCPS, is one way to protect yourself. Practitioner psychologists, who use titles such as clinical or counselling psychologist, must be registered with the HCPC.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Say whether you already have an ADHD diagnosis or are still exploring whether you might have ADHD.
Describe the main things you want help with, such as focus, routines, emotions or relationships.
Mention whether you would prefer to meet in person, and roughly where you are able to travel to.
Explain any preferences about the counsellor, such as experience with adults, young people or a particular approach.
Note whether you are looking for short-term support around a specific issue or something more open-ended.
Include anything that would help the counsellor understand your situation, such as work pressures or family circumstances.
questions_heading: Questions you could ask the counsellor
questions: What is your experience of working with people who have ADHD, and how does it shape your sessions?
Are you on a register accredited by the Professional Standards Authority, and which one?
Do you offer counselling in person near me, and where would sessions take place?
How would you describe your approach, and what would a first session involve?
How do you handle confidentiality, and what are its limits?
How do you work alongside any medical care I already have for ADHD?

faqs.q: Do I need a diagnosis before I can have ADHD counselling?
faqs.a: No, you do not need a diagnosis to see a counsellor. ADHD counselling and coaching can help before or after a diagnosis, and a counsellor can talk things through with you wherever you are in that process. Coaching is not a diagnosis, though, so if you want an assessment you would need to pursue that separately.

faqs.q: Is ADHD counselling the same as coaching?
faqs.a: They overlap but are not identical. Coaching tends to focus on practical strategies for organisation and daily life, while counselling often gives more room to emotions, relationships and how ADHD affects you. A good counsellor will explain their approach in the first session so you know what to expect.

faqs.q: How do I check that a counsellor is properly registered?
faqs.a: Ask which register they are on and whether it is accredited by the Professional Standards Authority. Registers such as BACP, UKCP or NCPS require training, supervision, a code of ethics and a complaints procedure. Practitioner psychologists using titles such as clinical or counselling psychologist must be registered with the HCPC.

faqs.q: Can counselling replace medication for ADHD?
faqs.a: No, medication is a separate medical decision made with a doctor or specialist, not something a counsellor provides. Counselling and coaching can sit alongside medical care and help with the practical and emotional side of living with ADHD. It is worth telling any counsellor about the care you already receive.
